text:
Response A is accurate but runs to roughly 145 words, well over the 120-word limit. Its only slip is calling the all-staff message an "email", when the source says "message". It keeps the key points: not a hack, scale, data exposed, regulator notification, the media leak, fixes and dates.

Response B fits the limit at about 107 words, but it contains a factual error. It says the job was stopped "after 35 minutes", when the source says it was stopped at 9:35am. The first call came in at 8:20am, so that is neither 35 minutes nor a clear duration. This is a misleading figure in a summary a manager will rely on. B also leaves out the media and communications issue, and the comms guide fix.

Accuracy ranks first, so B's wrong number counts against it. A's length overrun is a real failure of the brief, but its content is correct and more complete.

Verdict: A
